description: Authored starter knowledge for the botanical-garden scenario (nine flowers in two simulated rooms) plus a few COCO classes for webcam recognition. Curator-written general facts; replace with your own domain knowledge. Topic keys and keywords are matched as whole words.

rose.name: rose
rose.overview: This is a rose. Roses have been grown in gardens for thousands of years, and there are many hundreds of cultivated varieties.

care.text: Roses enjoy at least six hours of sun, well-drained soil and deep watering at the base rather than on the leaves.

meaning.text: Red roses are a classic symbol of love, while yellow roses usually stand for friendship and joy.

thorns.text: Careful: the sharp prickles on rose stems can scratch, so hold the stem gently.

tulip.name: tulip
tulip.overview: This is a tulip. Tulips grow from bulbs and bloom in spring with bright cup-shaped flowers.

care.text: Plant tulip bulbs in autumn, about three times as deep as the bulb is tall, in a sunny and well-drained spot.

history.text: In the seventeenth century tulips became so fashionable in the Netherlands that single bulbs sold for very high prices.

season.text: Tulips bloom in spring, usually between March and May.

sunflower.name: sunflower
sunflower.overview: This is a sunflower. Its large flower head is made of hundreds of tiny florets, and it can grow taller than a person.

care.text: Sunflowers love full sun and warm weather; water them deeply but not too often once they are established.

seeds.text: A single sunflower head can hold more than a thousand seeds, which birds and people both enjoy.

sun.text: Young sunflower buds turn to follow the sun across the sky; most mature flowers settle facing east.

orchid.name: orchid
orchid.overview: This is an orchid. Orchids form one of the largest flowering-plant families, with tens of thousands of species.

care.text: Most household orchids like bright indirect light and should be watered when their bark mix is almost dry.

roots.text: Many orchids grow on trees in the wild, and their silvery roots take moisture from the air.

lily.name: lily
lily.overview: This is a lily. Lilies grow from bulbs and have large trumpet-shaped flowers that are often fragrant.

care.text: Lilies like their flowers in the sun and their roots in cool, shaded, well-drained soil.

pets.text: Warning: lilies are toxic to cats, even in small amounts, so keep them away from pets.

daisy.name: daisy
daisy.overview: This is a daisy. What looks like one flower is really a cluster of tiny flowers: yellow ones in the centre and white petals around them.

care.text: Daisies are easy to grow in sunny spots and only need watering when the soil is dry.

name.text: The name daisy comes from the old English phrase for day's eye, because the flower opens in the morning and closes at night.

lavender.name: lavender
lavender.overview: This is lavender, a fragrant shrub with purple flower spikes from the Mediterranean region.

care.text: Lavender prefers full sun, poor well-drained soil and little water once it is established.

scent.text: Lavender's calming scent is used in soaps, perfumes and sachets, and bees love its flowers.

lotus.name: lotus
lotus.overview: This is a lotus, an aquatic plant whose flowers rise above the water on long stems.

leaves.text: Lotus leaves repel water so well that droplets roll off and carry dirt away, which is called the lotus effect.

meaning.text: In many Asian cultures the lotus is a symbol of purity, because it blooms clean from muddy water.

hibiscus.name: hibiscus
hibiscus.overview: This is a hibiscus, a tropical flower with large, colourful blossoms and a long central stamen.

care.text: Hibiscus likes warmth, plenty of light and regular watering; bring it indoors before frost.

tea.text: The dried calyces of one hibiscus species make a tart, ruby-red tea.

potted plant.name: potted plant
potted plant.overview: That looks like a potted plant. Detectors trained on everyday objects recognise plants in pots but not their species.

care.text: Most potted plants need drainage holes and should not stand in water.

vase.name: vase
vase.overview: That is a vase. Cut flowers last longer if you trim their stems and change the water every two days.

person.name: person
person.overview: I can see a person. This demo does not identify people or keep their images.

topics.privacy: Camera frames are processed by your local demo server only for the current question.

chair.name: chair
chair.overview: That is a chair. Feel free to rest while we talk.
